input.summary: R2 is implemented on the exact native03 subject: a stale immediate probe result no longer discards the still-valid immediate cleanup request. Starting hashes of all four targets and both tool pins matched SOURCE_SUBJECT/EXTERNAL_TOOLS. Delta across the four paths: (1) owned_process_lifetime.ts is unchanged (sha fbb571cc…, 265 lines/11,658 bytes); the synchronous bridge works as before. (2) owned_process_state.ts changed 237/13,490 -> 241/13,755 (sha 235fc19c…). In `probed`, a superseded `terminate-immediate` result still records no fact, never uses its stale absence and never runs its continuation; its immediate request alone is decided again by the ordinary `terminate(timing, s, "immediate", at)` rule against the current state. After completed cleanup nothing happens. In kill, after confirmed absence, or once KILL was already sent, nothing happens. In drain with unconfirmed absence it requests the one KILL. In term it enters kill through a fresh, counted probe whose current result decides KILL and the tighter deadline. No new state field, input, tail, wait, counter or bridge mechanism; R1 entry counting, coalescing, cancelled pre-entry tails, no-child/Windows assessment, clock/deadline, snapshot, Error and disposal/seal paths are byte-unchanged. (3) The test file went 977/69,020 -> 1031/72,946 (sha 222afb37…): two controlled actual-owner cases inserted after the kill-probe re-check case; all other test text is unchanged, giving 20 controlled timing/lifetime cases. Case one is the exact fixture (grace100, first probe emits exit(0,null) only, every later probe present, outer requestTermination('immediate')), run with the stale first result present and then absent. It requires KILL in the host census before the call returns, cleanupDeadlineNs at most 200ms, scopeAbsence still present, probeCount equal to census entries, every entry returned and signalAttempts equal to census signals; then frozen completion within 200ms, exactly one KILL, 3 disposals and no timers. Case two is outer immediate where the nested probe sees absence, then exit and close complete cleanup. It requires the stale outer result to arrive last with no signal, the immediate snapshot to deep-equal the frozen completion (absent, census count, 0 signals, 300ms bound), 3 disposals at handback, no timers, a later fresh snapshot with recomputed 25ms, a later immediate request causing no new calls, disposals or completions, and the same completion object. (4) The plan (63/20,144 -> 64/23,439) records: R1 source-satisfied with external proof pending; R2 an executed A regression with both discriminator results unchanged (pre-A TERM,KILL before return, 200ms, 6/6, pass; native03 TERM only, 300ms, 4/4, first KILL-before-handback assertion red, later KILL at 100ms and completion at 300ms as observation only); the correction that native03's 'as in native02 and the predecessor' is false for pre-A and later bounded completion does not discharge the immediate duty; a new R2 row; and accounting across both modules: lifetime 265/11,658 plus state 241/13,755 = 506 lines/25,413 bytes (241+203 = 444 non-blank, non-comment). That is +4/+265 over native03 and +208/+12,780 (+166 non-blank, non-comment) over pre-A. Coordination is unchanged: the bridge has two mutable bindings, a three-slot armed-wait record and three createMonotonicDeadline waits; the state has 15 facts plus waits and probing, 11 inputs, 4 tails and 5 continuations; R2 adds one conditional branch. It is consolidation, not net deletion. B, peer retained-fact proof and full Phase2 acceptance stay pending. The selfcheck asserts only KILL before handback, a deadline of at most 200ms and census equality.
